What we will change: History of campaigns and offers sent to each user, ideally with a control group
Why: The model predicts who will flip out, not who changes because of the campaign. A control group is needed to measure the real effect

Why: Declines and funding friction may explain why some users do not use the card outside OXXO

What we will change: Ranges of commission or margin by channel, and more months of history
Why: To estimate the CLV in the next stage with real values instead of team assumptions, and to train with more snapshots

What we will change: Volatility of the monthly OXXO share, number of non-OXXO purchases per month, days since the last non-OXXO purchase, cash funding ratio, spend trend
Why: The strongest drivers were related to the level and the recent change of the OXXO share; these features describe them better

What we will change: Creation flow, active months, PCA scores and persona as model inputs

What we will change: Test a threshold of 15 or 20 points, a minimum of 3 to 4 non-OXXO purchases per month, a 3-month persistence, or an increase in non-OXXO spend in pesos
Why: The event rate of about 35% and the importance of users with few purchases suggest that part of the events are random variation

What we will change: Exclude users with very few transactions in the observation window, or model them separately
Why: Their monthly shares change a lot by chance, which adds noise to the labels
